safePurpose: Prepare visibly separate questions for hepatitis B testing, qualified diagnosis and vaccination using age context, exposure timing category, testing record, diagnosis status and documented vaccination status.
privacy: Treat every selection as sensitive. Do not request actual laboratory values, names, clinic details, contact details, identifiers or vaccine batch data and do not store, log, upload, sync, email, add selections to accounts or URLs, or send them to analytics.
disallowed: interpreting a laboratory marker or marker combination
diagnosing, ruling out, verifying, classifying or staging hepatitis B
setting vaccine eligibility, doses or timing
using age or elapsed exposure time to delay exposure or prenatal care
staticText: Hepatitis B Testing, Qualified Diagnosis and Vaccination Pathway for /tools/hep-b-screening/. Keep all three conversations visibly separate. It may name HBsAg, anti-HBs and total anti-HBc for initial screening of adults aged 18 or older; route under-18 or unclear age contexts to age-specific professional guidance; distinguish a screening record, pending confirmation and a diagnosis already given by a qualified clinician; pass a possible-exposure timing category to the service without using it to decide action is too late; route pregnancy and possible recent exposure promptly; and prepare questions about documented vaccine history. Do not interpret markers, determine infection or immunity, diagnose, rule out, verify, classify or stage hepatitis B, set vaccine eligibility or timing, recommend treatment, or delay time-sensitive exposure or prenatal care. Do not request actual lab values, names, clinic details, identifiers or vaccine batch data. Selections are sensitive and local: do not store, log, upload, sync, email, add them to accounts or URLs, or send them to analytics. Sources reviewed 2026-07-26: WHO Hepatitis B fact sheet (10 June 2026), WHO consolidated implementation handbook (15 February 2026), and CDC Clinical Testing and Diagnosis for Hepatitis B.
